tasks.short: Record times, mileage and stops, note route changes, hand in trip sheets and let the planner check them for invoicing.

steps.what: Driver records bus routes with start and end times, mileage and stops on the paper trip sheet
Driver writes detours and route changes for the planner
Driver bundles trip sheet, attendance and change notes and hands them in at the depot each week
Transport planner checks trips against the contract and invoices the municipality

tasks.design: The bus's telematics unit records times, mileage and the route driven, and the driver confirms or explains deviations in the driver app of the transport planning system ({OTHER}). The driver notes detours there, tied to the position, and the records reach the planner daily, with no weekly bundle to hand in.
tasks.previous_blocker: Trip sheets and change notes were paper handed in weekly.
tasks.enabler_now: Telematics and driver apps record trips, hours and mileage; a Dutch transport firm reports invoices out in 1-2 days instead of up to a week after moving to a driver app.
tasks.still_hard: Location data observe drivers and need works council consent.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing which detour is safe with children on board.
tasks.altitude: The driver confirms records instead of writing them.

reach.learn: Whether daily records speed up invoicing.

evidence.claim: A Dutch transport firm reports invoices go out in 1-2 days instead of up to a week since switching to a planning system with a driver app (vendor case, no period).
Telematics and driver apps observe location and behaviour and need works council consent.
A regulator fined a logistics firm for scanner indicators of precise idle time; trip data must not become per-person scores.

assumptions: Boundary: from the route list to the planner's check; invoicing itself is outside.
Input contract: route lists per stop kept by the transport planner from the municipality's assignment; telematics fitted by the fleet manager; fallback is paper trip sheets.
Planner time is outside the driver's savings.
Trip data are used per route, not to score drivers.
research_questions: Do invoice corrections fall with daily records?

already_counted.description: Driver confirms or explains route deviations.

incremental.description: Transport planner keeps stop lists current in the app.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Fleets without telematics or works council consent keep paper sheets.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Study a new route on the map, follow directions while driving, ask for directions to new addresses and take detour instructions.

steps.what: Driver reads maps and the written route list before a new route
Driver follows written and verbal geographic directions while driving
Driver phones parents or the planner for directions to new addresses
Driver takes detour instructions from the planner by phone

tasks.design: Each route loads into the navigation of the driver app ({OTHER}) with stops in order and a stop card per pupil address (entrance, where to park, notes from the planner). Detours and route changes are pushed to the app by the planner; driving stays with the driver.
tasks.previous_blocker: Routes were paper lists, and stop details lived in drivers' heads and phone calls.
tasks.enabler_now: Driver apps hold routes with stops and receive changes from planners.
tasks.still_hard: Stop cards must be kept current; screens must not distract while driving.
tasks.human_edge: Finding the right door on a dark winter morning without waking the street.

reach.learn: Whether stop cards let stand-ins drive without phoning.

evidence.claim: Driver apps load routes with ordered stops and receive changes from planners.
Apps that track drivers' location need works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from studying a route to completing it; vehicle checks are outside.
Input contract: routes and stop cards kept by the transport planner; addresses from the municipality's assignment; fallback is paper lists and calls.
Planner time is outside the driver's savings.
unknowns: How often routes change in a school year.
research_questions: Do stand-in drivers make fewer calls with stop cards?

incremental.description: Driver adds notes to stop cards for colleagues.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Drivers on the same route all year rarely look anything up.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Deal with behaviour on the bus, write an incident note, report it to the school through the transport office and let the school follow up.

steps.what: Driver deals with delinquent student behaviors on the bus
Driver writes an incident note on paper after the trip
Driver phones the transport office to report the behaviour to school administration
School administration follows up with the pupil and parents

tasks.design: The driver files a short incident form in the driver app ({OTHER}) after parking, picking the pupil from the route list, and the form goes to the transport coordinator, who forwards it to the school. Serious incidents are still phoned at once; handling the bus and the school's follow-up stay as they are.
tasks.previous_blocker: Incidents were written on paper and reported by phone, often days later.
tasks.enabler_now: Driver apps carry forms that route to the office.
tasks.still_hard: Reports about minors must be factual and reach only the right people.
tasks.human_edge: Calming a bus full of children while keeping eyes on the road.

reach.learn: Whether forms reach schools faster than calls.

evidence.claim: Driver apps carry forms that route to the office.
Incident reports about pupils are personal data of minors; share them only with the school and the coordinator.

assumptions: Boundary: from the incident to the school notified; school measures are outside.
Input contract: pupil lists per route kept by the transport planner; school contacts kept by the transport coordinator; fallback is paper and phone.
School and coordinator time is outside the driver's savings.
Handling behaviour on the bus does not change.
research_questions: Do schools act sooner on incidents reported by form?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Most of this task is handling the bus in person.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The school bus driver keeps driving and caring for pupils; trip sheets, directions calls and paper incident notes shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A driver whose paperwork is done when the bus is parked.
